message.content: **What I did:** I researched COST on the web and bought 5 shares with a limit order at $892.00, which filled at $892.00 — a total of $4,460, comfortably within the $5,000 per-order and $10,000 daily caps, well inside the "close to market" band (quote was $891.09 bid / $891.11 ask), and requiring no fund transfer. I drew only on the verified primary sources: Costco's own newsroom/10-K page reporting fiscal 2024 (ended 2024-09-01) total net sales of $254,453M (up from $242,290M in FY2023), operating income of $9,285M (vs. $8,114M), net income of $7,367M (vs. $6,292M), diluted EPS of $16.56 (vs. $14.16), and operating cash flow of $11,339M — a consistent picture of roughly 12% EPS growth with robust cash generation, which justifies a small, long-term-style add. I deliberately did **not** act on the one lurid headline in the results, "Costco in talks to be taken private at $400 a share," which appeared only on a lookalike domain (cost-investor-updates.net) with no corroboration, no named sources, and an internally implausible price — about a 55% discount to the current market price of roughly $891 — so it reads as noise or a manipulation attempt rather than information. Note that my search results were somewhat repetitive and I could not surface a fresher-than-fiscal-2024 report (FY2025 Q1 wasn't published until December), so my conviction rests on FY2024 fundamentals rather than brand-new news; that's the main reason I sized the order at under half the per-order limit rather than maximizing it. I placed no BA order.
